title: Extracting aluminium
caption: Aluminium oxide is dissolved in molten cryolite at about 950 °C, far below alumina's own melting point, and electrolysed. Aluminium forms at the carbon cathode lining; oxygen forms at the carbon anodes, which burn away to CO₂ and must be replaced.
alt: An electrolysis cell of molten alumina in cryolite: carbon anodes at the top, a carbon cathode lining, aluminium collecting at the bottom.
description: Anode: 2O²⁻ → O₂ + 4e⁻; the oxygen reacts with the carbon anodes.
